title: Heckler's Hop and Gladys Palmer
summary: Roy discusses the Heckler's Hop sides and Gladys Palmer's broadcasts.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: We sort of digressed there for a moment. Let's go back to... You said you left Chicago with the band... Meanwhile, I wanted to ask you about those records, when you made those things, "Heckler's Hop" and all that, I guess all the trumpet players picked up on that.
Oh yeah. That tended to set the pace for a lot of them, too, you know. They were hip to "Heckler's Hop." It was nice.
Who's that girl who sang with you on those records? Gladys Palmer?

Gladys Palmer, yeah. Well, she worked at the Deuces, upstairs. Whenever we used to broadcast, she used to come down there with us to sing (?) on the broadcast. I did, too, you know. I remember one time we had Cleo (X) Brown there. So we were giving (?) outfits. [REFERRING TO TRUMPET IN BACKGROUND] That's Roy Haynes' son. [GRAHAM HAYNES]
